newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia builders say 96/97 forecast in doubt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia builders say 96/97 forecast in doubt.

text.p: Master Builders Australia said on Tuesday total building approvals needed to rise by around 17 percent over the next six months in order to meet a government forecast for about 128,000 dwelling units in the 1996/97 year.

National director, economics and housing, Wilhelm Harnisch said November's 1.6 percent drop in building approvals, seasonally-adjusted, was a blow to the housing industry as it pointed to a poor result for the first half of 1996/97.
"At the current level of building approvals, housing starts are only running at an annualised rate of around 118,000 dwelling units for 1996/97," Harnisch said in a statement.
He said this compared to 124,550 housing starts in 1995/96.
"It is estimated that total building approvals need to increase by around 17 percent over the next six months if housing activity is to reach the forecast level of 128,000 dwelling units," he said.
The Australian government's Indicative Planning Council predicted 127,200 total housing starts for the 1996/97 year in its October Housing Prospects Report, he said.
Harnisch said he expected the November and December interest rate cuts to have a positive impact on confidence and flow through into effective housing demand.
"Nevertheless, there remains a lack of confidence particularly among first home buyers who are still largely absent from the market," he said.
"The slowing in employment growth is contributing to a lack of confidence and is having a dampening effect on the housing recovery."
Australian dwelling unit building approvals fell to a seasonally-adjusted 10,942 in November from 11,121 in October, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said earlier on Tuesday.
Economists on average had expected building approvals to fall 2.0 percent. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
